answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry before it can vote or place offers. The registry permits one active account per locked token, and proven fraud burns the stake. A whisper from a fresh account thus has little influence unless backed by capital; spawning a thousand identities requires buying and immobilizing a thousand tokens. This does not stop a wealthy attacker, but it makes Sybil influence costly, ties the cost to scale, and leaves a public thread of deposits auditors can inspect. The haven is imperfect, not free.
